gap.missing_evidence: A cohort-linked transfer-ready/admission timestamp and physical ED departure timestamp, plus observation-cutoff status for ongoing boarders, are not present in the acquired public METEOR definitions. METEOR 799756 defines physical departure after an ED stay and states that a patient admitted to a ward or bed within the ED has not physically departed until leaving the ED. It does not define the transfer-ready/admission event, establish an empirical generic boarding-duration distribution, or provide patient-level elapsed times or censoring observations. The supplied R29 report recommends boarding as an observed outcome from transfer-ready/admission to physical departure, retaining ED occupancy until physical departure; no primitive duration or default is supported.
gap.owner: ED evidence coordinator; obtain approved linked patient-level EDC, admission/transfer-ready and current-census or bed-management data, with operational owners confirming event meanings and physical resource release.
gap.impact: Boarding may be represented as an elapsed outcome only when both event boundaries and cohort are observed. No generic boarding duration, distribution, hazard, or default can be calibrated from these definitions. Admission or transfer-ready status must remain distinct from physical ED departure; a boarder continues to occupy ED capacity until the operational location/resource release is recorded. Ongoing episodes at the observation cutoff must be right-censored rather than assigned zero duration or treated as completed. METEOR's departure definition alone does not establish the operational release timestamp or readiness event.
